one_liner: Pure-Rust, zero-unsafe YAML 1.2 serde library that parses config-sized documents to a Value 1.11-1.36x faster than yaml-rust2.
what_it_does: noyalib is a YAML 1.2 parser and serializer for Rust with serde binding (`from_str`, `from_slice`, `from_reader`, `to_string`), a dynamic `Value` enum, a zero-copy `BorrowedValue`, and a lossless CST (`cst::Document`) for edits that keep comments and layout. Its API is not compatible with yaml-rust2 (`YamlLoader`/`Yaml`); it follows the serde_yaml shape and ships a name-for-name serde_yaml 0.9 shim (the `compat-serde-yaml` feature or the `noyalib-serde-yaml` crate). The project reports 406/406 active cases passing on the official YAML test suite.
how_it_is_fast: The scanner hands out scalars as `Cow::Borrowed` when no escape forces a copy, and it finds delimiters with memchr's SSE2/NEON `memchr2`/`memchr3` plus a SWAR (8-byte `u64` stride) byte-set search for 4 or more needles. Integers are parsed by an 8-digits-per-`u64` SWAR decimal parser (measured 2.2-2.5x over `i64::from_str`), and the default `from_str` records no spans (docs: 34% less overhead). Typed `from_str::<T>` feeds parser events straight into the serde Visitor without building a Value AST (docs claim about 30% faster). The serializer's 3-4x lead over serde_yaml_ng comes from `itoa`/`ryu` direct-write buffers and fast detection of strings that need quotes.
when_to_use: Rust services that load config-sized YAML (a few KB to about 30 KB: Kubernetes manifests, GitHub Actions workflows, app config) into serde structs or a dynamic Value, where parse latency is worth 1.1-1.4x over yaml-rust2 or about 1.4-2.0x over serde_yaml_ng and serde-saphyr.
Workloads that emit a lot of YAML: serializing a Value measured 3.00-4.34x faster than serde_yaml_ng on 3-field and 20-field documents.
Moving off archived serde_yaml or deprecated serde_yml to a pure-Rust, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` crate. The compat shim and the per-crate migration guides make this cheaper.
Parsing untrusted YAML. `ParserConfig::strict()` and `ParserLimits` cap depth, aliases, nodes, document size and more, and the docs report that billion-laughs input is rejected in under 3 us.
no_std + alloc (with atomic pointers) or wasm32 targets, or tools that need fast parsing plus comment-preserving CST edits from one crate.
when_not_to_use: You need to beat libyaml, yaml-cpp or rapidyaml. None of them was measured. Derived from the page data, the parse-to-Value rate is about 32-64 MB/s on an M4, and the project's POLICIES.md gives about 36 MB/s for Value and 50-80 MB/s for typed parsing.
You already use yaml-rust2 and parsing is not a bottleneck. The 1.11-1.36x (M4) gain means an API rewrite: there is no drop-in layer and no yaml-rust2 migration guide.
Large documents. The comparison fixtures top out at 29 KB, and no MB-scale comparison against other crates is published.
Code that relies on typed mapping keys. `Value::Mapping` is `IndexMap<String, Value>`, so integer, bool and complex keys are converted to strings unless you use `MappingAny`.

Risk-averse production use. The crate has one main maintainer (OpenSSF Code-Review 0 per its own ECOSYSTEM.md), uses 0.0.x versions where a patch bump may break, and dozens of serializer and CST round-trip bugs were filed between 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-10 (all closed by 2026-09-16).

integration.dependencies: Always: serde_core, indexmap, rustc-hash, hashbrown, libm, memchr, smallvec. On by default and removable: itoa, ryu, serde_ignored. Opt-in: rayon, tokio, miette, schemars/jsonschema, figment, garde, validator, sval and others.
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.86.0 (edition 2024). The `nightly-simd` feature needs nightly `portable_simd`; the `compare-saphyr` bench needs 1.88+.
integration.platforms: any Rust target with no hand-written intrinsics (memchr SSE2/NEON plus portable SWAR). CI runs x86-64 Linux/macOS/Windows and aarch64 macOS/Linux; no_std builds for thumbv7em and riscv32imac; wasm32. Targets without atomic CAS (thumbv6m, AVR, MSP430) are unsupported.
integration.thread_safety: Documented: top-level functions are pure and can be called concurrently. Value, Mapping, Number, Spanned<T> and Error are Send + Sync. Spanned<T> deserialization uses a thread-local span context. The Rc-backed anchor registries are single-thread; the Arc variants are multi-thread.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — not source-compatible with yaml-rust2 (`YamlLoader::load_from_str` / `Yaml`). A serde_yaml 0.9 name-for-name shim exists (`compat-serde-yaml` feature or the `noyalib-serde-yaml` crate).

gotchas: `from_str` rejects multi-document input with a 'more than one document' error (since v0.0.29). Use `load_all_as` or `from_str_multi` where yaml-rust2's `load_from_str` returned every document.

The 4.2x / 9.2x `StructuralIter` result is a microbenchmark of a public primitive. `StructuralIter` does not appear in the scanner, scalar scanner or loader, so it does not contribute to the parse numbers, and the `simd` feature is a documented no-op.
YAML 1.2 semantics are the default: `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` stay strings and bare `0644` is not octal. `ParserConfig::version(YamlVersion::V1_1)` or the `legacy_*` flags opt back in.
In the 0.0.x series the patch number is the breaking-change axis, including changes to Value shape or scalar resolution. Pin exact versions: three releases shipped on 2026-09-22 alone.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only Rust YAML library among the catalogued siblings, so pick it over rapidyaml, libfyaml, fkYAML or yeptris when you are in Rust and want serde binding and safe code without a C/C++ build. Those C/C++ siblings publish MB/s results against yaml-cpp or libyaml, and noyalib has never been measured against them.
verified_claims_summary: The project's own criterion suite ran on an Apple M4 with Rust 1.95 stable (fat LTO, codegen-units=1, panic=abort) and parsed five fixtures (3-field doc to 29 KB 500-item list, plus a 4.4 KB k8s multi-doc) into a Value 1.11-1.36x faster than yaml-rust2's YamlLoader and 1.38-2.00x faster than serde_yaml_ng, yaml-spanned and serde-saphyr. A second dated run on an Apple A18 Pro with rustc 1.98 shows 1.21-3.31x over yaml-rust2 and 2.55-3.26x over serde-saphyr 1.2.0; neither run covers x86 or libyaml.
status_note: Actively developed (v0.0.51 on 2026-09-22), installs as an ordinary crate, and is dual MIT/Apache-2.0 per the README and Cargo.toml (the GitHub API lists only Apache-2.0), with 10 stars but about 541k crates.io downloads over the last 90 days.
